podcast.body: "Killing an Arab" caused riots and bans due to its title, despite the fact that the song was directly based on Albert Camus's novel *The Stranger* and carried an explicitly anti-racist message. The band received almost no financial compensation from the song due to contractual problems, meaning they suffered the controversy without any economic benefit. "Based on Camus's 'The Stranger' and conveying an anti-racist message, the band received almost no economic benefit due to contractual issues."

podcast.body: A 7-inch single released in early 1979 for "Killing an Arab." While the A-side was the same as the UK release, approximately 100 French promo copies featured a cover of the Jimi Hendrix classic "Foxy Lady" on the B-side, instead of the UK's "10:15 Saturday Night." These rare promo copies are valued at around $2,000. Michael Dempsey, The Cure's original bass player, handled lead vocals on this particular "Foxy Lady" recording, marking one of the very few instances where someone other than Robert Smith sang lead. "In 1979, a new band called the Cure released a 7-inch in France for killing an Arab on the A side, just like they did in the UK."
